q: Molecular biology is the branch of biology that seeks to understand the _____ basis of biological activity in and between cells.
e: Molecular biology focuses on the molecular basis of biological activity.

q: The study of chemical, physical structures, and functions of biological macromolecules is known as _____.
e: The study of biological macromolecules is molecular biology.

q: The main information-carrying molecules of the cell which direct the process of protein synthesis are _____.
e: Nucleic acids carry the genetic information for protein synthesis.

q: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and _____.
e: The two main classes are DNA and RNA.

q: DNA is the master blueprint for life and constitutes the genetic material in all free-living organisms and most _____.
e: DNA is the genetic material in most viruses.

q: RNA is the genetic material of certain viruses, but it is also found in all living cells, where it plays an important role in the making of _____.
e: RNA plays an important role in making proteins.

q: DNA is a double helix structure consisting of two _____ strands twine around each other.
e: DNA consists of two polynucleotide strands.

q: Each nucleotide in DNA is composed of a five-carbon deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group, and a _____ base.
e: DNA nucleotides contain a nitrogen-containing base.

q: The components of a DNA nucleotide are all linked together by _____ bonds.
e: The components of a nucleotide are linked by covalent bonds.

q: The purine bases in DNA are adenine (A) and _____.
e: The purine bases are adenine and guanine.

q: Purine bases have _____ fused rings in their chemical structures.
e: Purines have two fused rings.

q: The pyrimidine bases in DNA are cytosine (C) and _____.
e: The pyrimidine bases in DNA are cytosine and thymine.

q: Pyrimidine bases have a _____ ring in their chemical structure.
e: Pyrimidines have a single ring structure.

q: Each strand of DNA forms a backbone of alternating phosphate groups and _____.
e: The backbone consists of alternating phosphate groups and sugars.

q: In a DNA molecule, a purine molecule is always paired with a _____ molecule.
e: A purine always pairs with a pyrimidine.

q: Specifically, adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T) and guanine (G) always pairs with _____.
e: Guanine always pairs with cytosine.

q: The pairing of adenine with thymine and guanine with cytosine is called _____ base pairing.
e: This specific pairing is called complementary base pairing.

q: Hydrogen bonds link each complementary base pair. A and T are joined by _____ hydrogen bonds.
e: A and T are joined by two hydrogen bonds.

q: C and G are joined by _____ hydrogen bonds.
e: C and G are joined by three hydrogen bonds.

q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are _____, meaning the sugar molecules are oriented differently.
e: The two strands of DNA are antiparallel.

q: One strand of DNA lies in $5'$ to $3'$ direction and another strand in _____ direction.
e: The strands run in opposite directions, $5'$ to $3'$ and $3'$ to $5'$.

q: The $5'$ and $3'$ come from the numbering of the carbons on the _____ sugar.
e: The numbering comes from the deoxyribose sugar.

q: In a DNA strand, the phosphate group is on the _____ carbon.
e: The phosphate group is attached to the $5'$ carbon.

q: In a DNA strand, the OH group is on the _____ carbon.
e: The OH group is attached to the $3'$ carbon.

q: By convention, the sequence of a DNA strand is always written in the _____ direction.
e: DNA sequences are conventionally written $5'$ to $3'$.

q: Like DNA, RNA is a polymer of _____.
e: RNA is a polymer of nucleotides.

q: RNA contains four nucleotides with the bases adenine (A), uracil (U), cytosine (C), and _____.
e: RNA contains adenine, uracil, cytosine, and guanine.

q: Unlike DNA, RNA is _____.
e: RNA is typically single-stranded.

q: Which type of RNA can fold back on itself, and complementary base pairing within the same molecule stabilizes the looped structure?
e: tRNA folds back on itself to form a looped structure.

q: All RNA molecules are produced from a DNA template and are synthesized in the _____.
e: RNA is synthesized in the nucleus.

q: Messenger RNA (mRNA) acts as the template for _____.
e: mRNA acts as the template for translation.

q: Transfer RNA (tRNA) carries specific amino acid to mRNA at _____.
e: tRNA carries amino acids to the ribosome.

q: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) reads the _____ on mRNA.
e: rRNA reads the codon on mRNA.

q: In total, there are around _____ billion base pairs in the DNA of a typical mammalian cell.
e: A typical mammalian cell has around 3.2 billion base pairs.

q: The DNA molecule is a very stable structure which normally passes from generation to generation without change, and only rarely does it _____.
e: DNA rarely mutates.

q: The two separate strands of DNA are joined only with _____ bonds, which allow them to separate during DNA replication.
e: The strands are joined by hydrogen bonds.

q: By having the base pairs within the helical structure, the genetic information is protected from outside chemical and _____ forces.
e: The helical structure protects against chemical and physical forces.

q: DNA replication is made by a _____ method, which was predicted by Watson and Crick.
e: DNA replication is semiconservative.

q: The semiconservative method of DNA replication was proven by _____.
e: Meselson and Stahl proved the semiconservative method.

q: It is regarded as semiconservative because each resulting molecule consists of one old strand and one _____ strand.
e: Each new molecule has one old and one new strand.

q: Replication begins at special sites called origins of replication, where the replication _____ form.
e: Replication bubbles form at the origins of replication.

q: _____ enzymes unwind the double helix and unzip the two parental strands by breaking hydrogen bonds.
e: Helicase unwinds and unzips the DNA strands.

q: Genetic code is a set of rules for determining how genetic information is converted to an _____ sequence of a protein.
e: The genetic code converts nucleotide sequences to amino acid sequences.

q: The genetic code defines a code specifying the relationship between a nucleotide codon and an _____.
e: It specifies the relationship between a codon and an amino acid.

q: Researchers knew that there are only four nucleotides in RNA, but _____ different kinds of amino acids.
e: There are 20 different kinds of amino acids.

q: The minimum combination of the four nucleotides was a triplet code, which could produce _____ possible combinations.
e: A triplet code produces 64 possible combinations.

q: The triplet hypothesis proposed that the genetic code consists of a combination of three nucleotides, called a _____.
e: A combination of three nucleotides is called a codon.

q: Between 1961 and 1965, various research groups compared artificially synthesized RNA molecules with the amino acid sequences of _____.
e: They compared RNA sequences with polypeptide sequences.

q: By convention, the genetic code is always interpreted in terms of the _____ codon rather than the DNA sequence.
e: The code is interpreted in terms of the mRNA codon.

q: The genetic code is _____, meaning that more than one codon can code for the same amino acid.
e: The genetic code is redundant.

q: There are only _____ codons that do not code for any amino acid and serve as stop signals.
e: There are three stop codons.

q: The genetic code is _____, meaning it reads as a series of three-letter codons without spaces or overlap.
e: The genetic code is continuous.

q: A shift of _____ nucleotides in either direction can alter the codon groupings and result in an incorrect sequence.
e: A shift of one or two nucleotides alters the reading frame.

q: The genetic code is nearly _____, meaning almost all organisms build proteins with the same genetic code.
e: The genetic code is nearly universal.

q: The universality of the genetic code means that a codon in the fruit fly codes for the _____ amino acid as in a human.
e: A codon codes for the same amino acid across almost all organisms.

q: The universality of the genetic code has important implications for gene technology, such as _____.
e: Universality allows for gene cloning across species.

q: A gene taken from one organism and inserted into another kind of organism will produce the _____ protein.
e: It will produce the same protein due to the universal code.

q: Which of the following is a start codon that also codes for the amino acid methionine?
e: AUG is the start codon for methionine.

q: Which of the following amino acids is coded by the start codon AUG?
e: AUG codes for methionine.

q: UAA, UAG, and UGA are _____ codons that serve as stop signals to end protein synthesis.
e: UAA, UAG, and UGA are terminator codons.

q: The two steps in protein synthesis are transcription and _____.
e: Protein synthesis involves transcription and translation.

q: In transcription, mRNA is synthesized based on the DNA template of a _____.
e: mRNA is synthesized from a gene template.

q: Translation involves the production of a protein with an amino acid sequence based on the _____ sequence.
e: Translation is based on the mRNA sequence.

q: The central dogma of molecular biology stated that genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to _____.
e: Information flows from DNA to RNA to Protein.

q: Transcription occurs in the _____ of the cell.
e: Transcription occurs in the nucleus.

q: There are three defined stages in the transcription process; initiation, elongation, and _____.
e: The stages are initiation, elongation, and termination.

q: For each gene, only one strand of the double-stranded DNA molecule is transcribed, called the _____ strand.
e: The transcribed strand is the antisense or template strand.

q: The strand of DNA which is not transcribed is called the sense strand or _____ strand.
e: The non-transcribed strand is the coding strand.

q: The sense strand has the same sequence as the product mRNA, with thymine instead of _____.
e: DNA has thymine where mRNA has uracil.

q: During elongation, RNA polymerase synthesizes mRNA complementary to the template strand in the _____ direction.
e: mRNA is synthesized in the $5'$ to $3'$ direction.

q: When the RNA polymerase reaches the termination signal, they _____ from the DNA strand.
e: RNA polymerase detaches at the termination signal.

q: The newly synthesized mRNA is called precursor mRNA or _____.
e: Newly synthesized mRNA is pre-mRNA.

q: Before moving to the cytoplasm, modifications convert pre-mRNA to _____ mRNA.
e: Pre-mRNA is converted to mature mRNA.

q: The first modification of pre-mRNA is the addition of a $5'$ cap at the _____ end.
e: A cap is added at the $5'$ end.

q: A poly-A tail consisting of 100-200 _____ nucleotides is added at the $3'$ end.
e: A poly-A tail consists of adenine nucleotides.

q: During mRNA modification, introns which are _____ regions are removed.
e: Introns are non-coding regions.

q: During mRNA modification, the remaining _____ which are coding regions are joined.
e: Exons are the coding regions that are joined.

q: In splicing, snRNA forms base-pairs with the $5'$ end of intron and at the _____ site.
e: snRNA pairs at the branch site.

q: snRNPs associate with other factors to form a _____ which excises the intron.
e: snRNPs form the spliceosome.

q: The second stage of protein synthesis involves translation which occurs in the _____.
e: Translation occurs in the cytoplasm.

q: Translation is the conversion of a sequence of nucleotides into a sequence of _____ in the polypeptide chain.
e: Translation converts nucleotides to amino acids.

q: The mature mRNA is attached at the _____ subunit of the ribosome.
e: mRNA attaches to the small ribosomal subunit.

q: There are three binding sites for tRNA on the large subunit: A site, P site and _____ site.
e: The binding sites are A, P, and E.

q: Opposite to the acceptor stem of tRNA is the _____ which connects to the specific codon.
e: The anticodon connects to the mRNA codon.

q: Scientists can use genetically modified organisms to profile the DNA sequence of a _____ tumour.
e: GMOs can profile DNA of cancerous tumours.

q: Genetic engineering is the alteration of the _____ material of an organism in a specific manner.
e: Genetic engineering alters genetic material.

q: Transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals are commonly referred to as genetically modified organisms, or _____.
e: They are referred to as GMOs.

q: A transgenic organism is produced from the introduction of foreign DNA into its genome, providing it with a new _____.
e: Foreign DNA provides a new phenotype.

q: Recombinant DNA is a method of transferring a gene into the genome of another organism of different _____.
e: It transfers genes between different species.

q: In order to insert the recombinant gene into a target cell, a _____ is needed.
e: A vector is needed to insert the gene.

q: Which of the following can be used as a vector to insert recombinant DNA?
e: Plasmids can act as vectors.

q: Vitamin A deficiency can cause blindness and an _____ deficiency syndrome.
e: It causes an immune deficiency syndrome.

q: The genes for beta-carotene in Golden Rice come from daffodils and _____ bacteria.
e: The genes come from daffodils and Erwinia bacteria.

q: The genes for making beta-carotene are inserted into plasmids that occur inside _____.
e: Plasmids occur inside Agrobacterium.

q: Agrobacteria are added to a petri dish containing rice _____.
e: They are added to a dish containing rice embryo.

q: Substituting the gene from daffodils plant with one from _____ gave higher quantities of carotene.
e: Substituting with a maize gene gave higher quantities.

q: Golden Rice contains the orange pigment _____ which can be converted into vitamin A.
e: It contains the pigment beta-carotene.

q: One benefit of genetic engineering of crops is increased resistance to pests and _____.
e: Crops gain resistance to pests and pathogens.

q: Genetic engineering of crops can lead to enhanced food quality due to slower _____.
e: It enhances quality due to slower spoilage.

q: Since the mid-1980s, medicinal products such as human growth hormone and _____ have been produced in transgenic plants.
e: Transgenic plants produce antibodies.

q: One type of antibody made by transgenic corn can deliver _____ to tumour cells.
e: Antibodies from corn deliver radioisotopes.

q: An antibody made by transgenic soybeans can be used to treat genital _____.
e: Soybean antibodies treat genital herpes.

q: To produce transgenic animals, a foreign gene is inserted into the genome of an animal _____ that is then fertilized.
e: The gene is inserted into an oocyte.

q: After the oocyte is fertilized, it is implanted in a host female and allowed to _____.
e: The fertilized egg is allowed to develop.

q: Transgenic animals can produce human proteins using a recombinant _____ vector.
e: They use a recombinant plasmid vector.

q: The vector contains a promoter that directs the expression of the genes in _____ cells.
e: The promoter directs expression in mammary cells.

q: In the production of GM sheep, the human hormone gene is cloned next to a sheep _____ promoter.
e: It is cloned next to the $ eta$-lactoglobulin promoter.

q: GM animals can be used for the production of organs for transplantation, known as _____.
e: Organ production for transplantation is xero-transplantation.
